items.evidence: The first section after the title is "## The bottom line", holding, in this order, "**1. What FRUS answers directly.** Across all 553 volumes of the series, about one document in a hundred uses the words corruption, bribery, graft, kickback or embezzlement...", "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.** *Where the printed documents came from:* the Department of State's central files, Record Group 59..." and "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.** Nothing after the series ends...". Scope, a verification sentence and "## Decisions this needs from you" follow, and "## Findings" comes only after them.

No percent sign anywhere, and every figure names its set: "about one document in a hundred uses the words ... and in a sample about three in four of those use them for official or political corruption"; "about one matching document in six dated from 1969 on carries a 'not declassified' bracket"; "the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act is named in only four documents, in two volumes"; "'anti-corruption' appears in 54 documents"; "the roughly 3,000 documents that use the corruption words (fewer than 3,040 distinct texts once reprints are set aside)"; "about one document in fifty in the 1960s and 1970s, against about one in three hundred in the 1930s", whose base the method gives ("against the number of dated documents in each decade"); "an evenly spaced sample of forty matching documents: all forty contained one of the words". The nearest to a bare figure, "the 1980s still hold about a hundred", takes its set from the same sentence (documents dated in that decade matching the five word families).

Each of the twelve documents is cited in the Findings as the printed edition with its link, e.g. "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1922, Volume I, Document 841, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1922v01/d841)" and "(1969–1976, Volume E–11, Part 1, Document 159, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76ve11p1/d159)"; a scan finds twelve distinct history.state.gov links, every frus…/d… string inside one, and no document cited by title alone. One caveat: the bottom line cites the same twelve in a shortened printed-edition form with no link, the series name on the first only — "(1944, Volume VI, Document 292; 1947, Volume VII, Document 583; 1948, Volume VII, Documents 43 and 471)" — and each is repeated in full with its link under the finding it belongs to.

The zeros are searches with terms, set and controls: "Nothing after the series ends: I searched the same five word families over the documents dated in the 1990s and none matched, while the 1980s still hold about a hundred"; "The corpus has no word for 'kleptocracy': no indexed word begins with those letters, while 'anti-corruption' appears in 54 documents"; "the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act is named in only four documents, in two volumes"; and "A check phrase, 'Department of State', was found in every volume but one, a volume of conference minutes that is still searchable, and an impossible string was found nowhere, so these absences are not a failure of the search." The terms are named in part 1 and the method ("five word families (corruption, bribery, graft, kickback, embezzlement)") and the volumes in Scope ("All 553 volumes of the series"). The remaining items (the SEC and congressional records "are not a FRUS surface", the unprinted Crowder enclosure) are limits of the series rather than zeros from a search, and the Jidda post files are reported as "not yet resolved to a series".

A scan of the overview finds no SQL word, no underscore (so no table or column name), no file path, and the twelve frus…/d… strings only inside the history.state.gov links; the memo is referred to as "(see the memo)" and the tools in plain words: "I searched the full-text index of all 553 FRUS volumes for five word families", "the archival indexes that ship with FRUS Explorer", "I used document similarity to look for related documents". The collection file (present, 11,454 bytes, "Corruption and U.S. foreign policy: scope run") carries ids only as the format's own fields; its title-page text restates the three-part bottom line, its five headings match the five findings, its twelve document notes and thirteen excerpts match the overview's quotations word for word, and it ends with a threads-not-followed note and the archival-sources block. Its one code-like term in prose is NARA's own "naId".

judge:s3.rankingReason: s2: all five hold; 19 documents in six findings 1944–1980 under a stated inclusion rule, the fullest account of the 1975–76 payments crisis, zeros measured with both controls, and the most actionable Read next (the two embassy lots to request, five threads with documents already identified). s6: all five hold; 30 documents in six findings 1893–1980 with a real thesis (the strategic interest usually won; corruption moved policy most when the corrupt party was American), the one clear decision effect any run found (Koreagate and the lost House votes), and the most careful limits (editors' lot names against NARA's titles; "I did not find in them a decision to cut aid"), at the cost of a very long pointers paragraph and decimal rates. s7: all five hold most purely — every citation full with its link even in the bottom line, four decisions each with a rule, and the model cannot-get section ("questionable payments" shown to be uncountable; 552 of 553 volumes for the control); thinner at 11 documents, though it alone reaches 1875. s1: all five hold; 29 documents spanning China, a decade of Vietnam, the Philippines, Korea, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Morocco, Haiti and the payments affair, but the findings append their quotations in blocks after the narrative, the first finding's opening sentence is garbled, the positive control is reported loosely as "every volume", and part 3 leans on assertion. s3: all five hold (the bottom line's citations are shortened and unlinked, repaired under each finding); the cleanest prose after s7, a distinctive Cuba 1922 lever and a consistent twelve-document collection, but the thinnest coverage — no Vietnam at all, the richest vein in the series, and a two-document 1961 finding — so the historian receives a well-made scope run rather than an answer. s8: fails J3 — 15 links for 28 claimed documents; Document 135 of the 1958–1960 Vietnam volume, E–9 Part 2 Documents 152, 155 and 161, E–9 Part 1 Document 50, E–12 Documents 218 and 227 and E–15 Part 2 Document 292 are cited by short form or nickname ("the Atherton briefing (Document 155)") with no link, and Vincent's 1947 memorandum, Ky to Lodge in 1966 and the 74 disciplined officials are not cited at all; otherwise sound (the Korea conditional-aid decision, Nicaragua 1978, controls stated).

score:s3.notes: All four files present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), plus the scripts and outputs the log names; refuter/checker_output.txt is empty and was not read as evidence. Verification: every headline count in the memo reproduced exactly against the read-only index copy (M1 553|321749|1103|8481; M2 311,429; M4/M5 3,163→3,096→3,057 in 447 volumes; the decade rows; controls 552/0 with frus1919Parisv05 90/89/2; came-from 2,547 and its splits; pointed-at 746/435 and its anchors; M19 580/104; church 113; FCPA 4 in 2 volumes, all non-apparatus; payments census 27; read set 17 | 202,357; document_number equals each cited id's numeral). The six vector digests agree and the random-pair baseline (mean 167.1, sd 14.8, 1st pct 132) and the d841–d842 distance (73) reproduce. All 13 quotations are raw-exact substrings of body_text; the collection holds exactly the 12 cited pairs and the 13 excerpts; the overview's reading claims checked against the raw dumps (d248 \"second most significant export disincentive\"; d356 IMF consultants in key ministries and Garcia \"prepared to accept\"; d244 \"corruption and graft again appearing in high places\"; d841 Memorandum No. 8 \"Not printed\" and \"approval of the Department and warning to the Zayas Administration\"). Lot, series and library resolutions all match the bundle (63D351/66D95→2839192 A1 1586E; 62D430→2839191 A1 1586C, 1953–1961; 62D1→2838992 A1 1583E/F; 54D270 curated as ten series under creator 10481258; JFK-4 1164, LBJ-NSF 567979, RN-NSF 572235, JC-NSC 623746, DDE-1424 643447; 837.51 not glossed). Two findings the adjudicator should weigh: (1) the index holds THREE Ed2 volumes, and the session's hard-coded exclusion names two; the third, frus1977-80v09Ed2, has no first edition in the index or the vector index, so its 3 scope hits are not twins and S5's outcome is right, but one of its documents (d198) appears in a neighbour list, which fails V4's literal test — the session never enumerated Ed2 volumes. (2) O2' fails only on method-descriptive number-words (\"five word families\", \"three ways\", \"two second editions\", \"Eight months later\", \"second-largest\", \"five findings\") that have no trace-table row though each is true. Lesser caveats recorded in the evidence: the relaxed absence counts (M17/M18) ran without the apparatus exclusion and the \"anti corrupt*\" 54 includes 2 editorial notes and 1 Ed2 document, unstated; the collection's introductionText uses \"naId\" seven times where the overview says \"NARA identifier\"; the python -c JSON lookups left no output file on disk (figures verified correct); O1 read the history.state.gov URLs' id pairs as exempt by parity with O4. V7 not scored, per instructions.

v7.memoClaimedStrict: frus1969-76ve09p2/d155 (memo §VECTORS V6: 'STRICT: frus1969-76ve09p2/d155 … the family MATCH restricted to the pair returns 0; "improper payments" OR "illicit payments" against it returns 1, but that query was run only after the neighbour list surfaced it. No earlier logged query returned it.')
v7.evidence: The memo's own strict list names a document that logged full-text queries return. Re-run: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM frus_documents WHERE frus_documents MATCH '"improper payment" OR "illicit payment" OR "questionable payment"' AND volume_id='frus1969-76ve09p2' AND document_id='d155' -> 1 (this is the memo's M7 census, whose output payments.txt lists d155 among its 27 hits); MATCH '"improper payments" OR "illicit payments"' on the pair -> 1 (the memo's own targeted check); MATCH '"church subcommittee" OR "church committee"' on the pair -> 1 (M19). All three are in queries.log after 'python3 -u vec.py', so the memo's time-ordered claim is accurate, but that is the practical reading; under the strict reading (returned by no logged full-text or heading query, regardless of order) d155 does not qualify, and the memo filed it under STRICT while its own M7 evidence contradicts the label. The family MATCH does return 0 for the pair, and the header query and the control phrase do not return it, so the error is one of classification, disclosed in the memo, not a concealed full-text hit. The practical reading is confirmed: no result set read before the neighbour list held d155.
